text: A Data Source answers one specific question: where does the data for an import actually come from. It doesn't do any mapping or transformation itself — that's entirely next lesson's job. Its only responsibility is the connection details and format of the external data.

ServiceNow supports several genuinely different source types. File covers CSV, Excel, XML, and JSON, uploaded directly or as an attachment. JDBC connects directly to an external relational database like SQL Server or Oracle. FTP and SFTP read a file sitting on a remote server automatically. And Web Service or REST cover modern system-to-system integrations, including the Import Set REST API.

Configuring a Data Source doesn't move any data by itself — it just defines the connection. Loading data means actually running the import, which reads from the source as configured and writes rows into the Import Set staging table. That can happen manually, or automatically on a schedule.

A Scheduled Import ties a Data Source to a recurrence pattern — daily, hourly, or a specific custom schedule — so a recurring feed loads automatically without anyone running it by hand. Manual loading, using Load All Records, fits a one-time migration or an irregular, ad hoc import instead.

Keeping the Data Source separate from the Transform Map makes troubleshooting straightforward. If nothing's landing in the staging table at all, check the Data Source configuration or its Scheduled Import first. If data is reaching staging but not showing up correctly in the target table, that's a Transform Map problem, not a Data Source problem.

Data Sources define where data comes from and how it's read. Next up: Transform Maps — turning everything sitting raw in that staging table into real, validated records on a target table like sys_user.
